primary_evidence.role: exact RawDataProcessor QByteArray transform and imported Qt identities
accepted TIODeviceWriter/QDataStream helper identity and byte-order configuration support

proven_facts: Current main PR #492 canonically proves the same outbound QByteArray/message reaches TGameserverTCPConnection::write at 0xb40a10 and then QDataStream::writeRawData at 0x4dd250 on a concrete TGameserverTCPConnection-owned QTcpSocket.
At 0xf50090 the canonical message is retained in rbp and its QByteArray size is loaded from message+0x18.

Before the raw payload write, 0xf500c6..0xf500f7 computes ceil(payload_length/8) for nonnegative payload lengths, forwards its low 16-bit value through the writer scalar slot, and writes it to the same underlying QDataStream.
Next, 0xf50107..0xf50121 loads a 32-bit scalar from message+0 and writes it through the next writer scalar slot to the same underlying QDataStream.
Only after those two scalar writes, 0xf5013d..0xf50153 forwards the payload pointer and payload length preserved from message+0x8/+0x18 into QDataStream::writeRawData at 0x4dd250.

The exact RawDataProcessor at 0xb47130 prepends one byte, appends bytes until the QByteArray length is divisible by 8, stores the number of appended bytes in the first byte, and assigns the transformed QByteArray back to the same message.

The existence and order of two deterministic pre-payload scalar writes on the already-proven QTcpSocket-bound QDataStream is sufficient to prove an outbound framing layer at this boundary without assigning semantic names to those scalars.
